sentences.text: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Wasim Sadiq Nargal, Judge

1. Through the medium of instant petition, the petitioners seek the following reliefs:-
"WRIT OF MANDAMUS (i) Commanding upon the respondents to acquire the land of the petitioners, illegally occupied by the respondents falling under Khasra No. 461 min, 462 min, Khewat No.
75, Khata No. 882, 883 and 884, total measuring 18-20 Kanals situated at Rakh Dhok, Jourian, Akhnoor, Jammu.

(ii) Further Commanding upon the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioners as per prevailing market rate and in terms of Acquisition Policy adopted by the Government of India in terms of land compensation."

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners are owners of the land falling under Khasra No. 461 min, 462 min, Khewat No. 75, Khata No. 882, 883 and 884 total measuring 18-20 kanals situated at Rakh Dhok, Jourian, Akhnoor, Jammu.

3. It is submitted by the petitioners that the illegal act of the respondents is evident from the fact that the respondents did not adopt any acquisition proceedings and divested the petitioners from their livelihood and the petitioners are starving since then to earn their livelihood.
More so, the petitioners have been relegated to the verge of vagrancy because of illegal act and conduct of the respondents and has been striving since then for justice.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that after exhausting all the remedies available to the petitioners, the petitioners applied under RTI wherein asking "when and under what orders the ancestral land of Manga Ram and his legal heirs falling under Khasra No. 461 min, 462 min, Khewat No. 75, Khata No. 882, 883 and 884, total measuring 18-20 kanals situated at Rakh Dhok, Jourian,
Akhnoor, Jammu have been acquired" and whether notice was issued to the owners of land of Manga Ram and legal heirs, but the reply clearly depicted that "no such file of acquisition is available in this office".
5. Learned counsel for the petitioners further submits that subsequent to receiving of the reply in RTI, the petitioners have once again represented their grievance before the respondents by way of representation but no action has been initiated by the respondents to mitigate the grievances of the petitioners, as such the petitioners are approaching this Court to mitigate their genuine right and demands regarding compensation as guaranteed by the Constitution.
Feeling aggrieved of what has been stated above, the petitioners have approached this Court by way of instant writ petition.

6. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners would feel satisfied, if the instant writ petition is disposed of by directing the respondents to treat the instant writ petition as representation and accord consideration to the same within some reasonable period.

7. Issue notice to the respondents.
8.

Mr. S. S. Nanda, learned Sr. AAG waives notice on behalf of the respondents No. 1 & 2, Mr. K. D.
S. Kotwal, learned Dy. AG on behalf of the respondent No. 3 and Ms. Priyanka Bhat, learned counsel appearing vice Mrs. Monika Kohli, learned Sr. AAG on behalf of the respondent No. 4.

They submit that the respondents have no objection, if the instant writ petition is directed to be treated as representation and same is accorded consideration strictly in accordance with the rules and as per law.

9. With the consent of learned counsel for the parties and keeping in view the facts and circumstances of the case, the instant writ petition is disposed of, at the threshold, with a direction to the respondents to consider the claim of the petitioner by treating this writ petition as representation and take a decision thereon, strictly under rules and as per law and pass a consideration order within a period of six weeks from the date a certified copy of this order alongwith complete set of writ petition are made available to the respondents.
